input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: The truthiness check `if fg:` (and likewise `if bg:` at line 684) drops valid color 0, so style(text, fg=0) emits no color code instead of the black ANSI code.
- rationale: Trigger: a caller passes fg=0 or bg=0, which are valid palette indices. The old `is not None` check emitted \033[38;5;0m. The new truthiness check skips the color entirely. Impact: the styled text silently loses its color with no error.
critique: The finding points to the same cause as the label: `if fg:` / `if bg:` truthiness checks skip the valid 256-color index 0. It also gives the same result, with fg=0 or bg=0 silently emitting no color code.
